subject: MAP: acceptance tests, exit gates & decision ledger
messages:
From: Amy Chen <amy.chen@carebridge.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: CareBridge Procurement <procurement@carebridge.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T13:12:00-07:00
Subject: Defining the MAP acceptance tests and exit gates

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency and the privacy controls. Before we move to a pilot commit, procurement and our SRE leads asked for a concrete acceptance test ledger tied to the MAP so they can sign off. Specifically they want: 

- A small set (4–6) of deterministic acceptance tests with owners and pass thresholds
- Clear go / no-go exit gates (what fails the trial)
- Expected evidence/artifacts we must provide for each test (logs, query samples, perf traces)
- A single place (spreadsheet or doc) that maps MAP milestones to tests and signoff owners

I attached a quick draft of what runs through procurement (MAP-Acceptance-Test-Matrix.xlsx) — it's skeletal and missing thresholds. Can your team fill thresholds and owners? Also can you confirm whether Redwood will run the smoke/perf tests or if CareBridge should run them in our environment?

We'll need this doc finalized for our steering committee on Aug 27 (internal) and then procurement needs the artifact for the legal playbook.

Thanks,
Amy Chen
Director, Product Ops — CareBridge

Attachments: MAP-Acceptance-Test-Matrix.xlsx
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Chen <amy.chen@carebridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-21T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Defining the MAP acceptance tests and exit gates

Hi Amy — appreciate the clarity and the deadline. We looked over your spreadsheet and sketched a proposed acceptance ledger. Key points up front: 

1) Ownership: Redwood will own provider-side smoke tests (model correctness, host latency, KV cache validity). CareBridge will run integration/throughput tests in your staging VPC (network egress, auth/KMS flows). We will jointly witness final verification.

2) Minimum acceptance test set (proposed):
   - Functional conformance: 100 sample prompts from your dataset; >95% label-match to golden set (CareBridge owner: Amy Chen; Redwood owner: Soojin Lee)
   - Latency SLA: 95th percentile < 350ms on inference path at trial QPS baseline (owner: Karthik Iyer)
   - Throughput scaling: End-to-end pipeline supports X requests/min with <20% tail degradation during burst (owner: CareBridge SRE — procurement contact to provide rep)
   - Data residency/audit: Evidence of audit log ingestion and retention policy applied to trial data (owner: Marissa Cole)

3) Exit gates (fail-fast rules):
   - Any single security control (KMS integration, VPC egress policy) failing verification by signoff date = automatic pause (procurement/sre review)
   - Functional failure: >10% of prompts outside tolerance for 3 consecutive runs = fail and requires remediation window
   - Latency regression: 95th percentile latency increase >30% vs baseline under identical load = fail

4) Evidence artifacts: sample prompts and responses, perf traces (Flame graphs), token-level cost report, audit log dump (last 30 days), and DocuSign-signed acceptance checklist.

5) Timeline & decision path: we propose a 5-day joint verification window starting Aug 24, Redwood provides provider-side test reports by Aug 25, CareBridge runs staging verification Aug 25–26, joint signoff Aug 27. If any exit gate trips, a 72-hour remediation window is enacted; if unresolved, we escalate to execs per MAP.

I've attached our annotated copy of your matrix and added owners/threshold suggestions. Soojin and Karthik — can you review owners/thresholds and raise any strong objections before I send this back to Amy?

Best,
Logan Wright
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-Acceptance-Test-Matrix.xlsx (annotated)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Amy Chen <amy.chen@carebridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Defining the MAP acceptance tests and exit gates

Thanks — quick clarifications from engineering and an updated checklist link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example-MAP

- Functional conformance: we'll run the Redwood-side sampling against the golden set and deliver a confusion log. CareBridge should confirm the golden labels and provide the 100-sample seed list by EOD Aug 23.
- Latency SLA: our 95th < 350ms target assumes model variant XQ-2 and a warm KV cache (cold-starts excluded). If you want to test with cold-start conditions we should add a separate cold-start test.
- Throughput scaling: please confirm expected baseline QPS for the trial (we put 20 QPS in the matrix as a placeholder).
- Evidence packaging: we'll provide perf traces and token-cost CSV. For audit logs we need the retention window you expect; current default is 90 days.

Owners (final):
- Redwood: Soojin (functional sampling), Karthik (perf/latency), Marissa (audit/retention evidence)
- CareBridge: Amy (golden set & integration runs), CareBridge SRE (throughput owner)

I'll update the matrix in the Drive and tag owners. Amy — once you drop the seed set I'll run provider-side samples and post the results in the shared Drive.

On governance: we recommend a single-row acceptance ledger at the top of the MAP that lists the final pass/fail values and the signoff cell with the approver's name + timestamp (DocuSign optional). That keeps procurement happy and makes rollbacks explicit.

- Soojin
Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
